newsitem.title: UK: Euroshares, dollar chase Wall Street higher.
newsitem.headline: Euroshares, dollar chase Wall Street higher.

text.p: European shares chased Wall Street higher on Friday when the U.S. market surged about one percent, a move which also prompted the dollar to rise.
Europe's three key bourses, London, Frankfurt and Paris, closed up 0.8, 1.5 and 1.1 percent, respectively, recouping about half of the steep losses made on Thursday.

Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average was up more than 60 points at the end of European trading, with technology stocks leading the way as they rebounded from their recent woes and outperformed the rest of the market.
European shares romped higher in early trade after Wall Street recovered from being 96 points down on Thursday to close with a loss of just 5.78 points.
Friday's Wall Street surge was a continuation of strong buying seen late on Thursday as programme buying kicked in.
But U.S. shares remained prey to fears that too rapid growth in the world's number one economy might lead to higher interest rates, which would undermine soaring share valuations, however.
Stronger-than-expected U.S. construction spending in November, which the Commerce Department said rose 1.9 percent, were shrugged off however.

In London, Europe's largest bourse closed up 32.1 points at 4089.5, though volume was thin with many players still on holiday. The underlying mood was also cautious with most strategists not expecting the FTSE 100 index to repeat its near 12-percent growth in 1997.

According to a survey of pension funds published by the WM Company this week, fund managers are running higher cash positions and have already reduced their exposure to British equities in the belief that stocks are overvalued.
"We're in the final stages of the bull market," said Chris Chaitow, a technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.
"Whether we can go up another 100 points is hard to predict," he said. "But I'm working on the theory that the next major market move will be down...January may turn out to be disappointing."
French stocks also followed U.S. shares up, extending their earlier gains and the blue-chip CAC-40 index, which traded nervously in the morning, closed higher 25.79 points at 2,282.76.

Germany's electronically traded Ibis DAX index rose 42.45 points to 2,863.26 points, boosted by interest from German domestic fund managers and a strong performance from German Bunds, as well as Wall Street.
Floor trade on Germany's DAX-30 index ended at 2,859.28 points, showing a gain of 10.51 points. Because the index closes early it does not mirror Wall Street's gyrations blow for blow.

In currencies, the dollar recovered during a quiet European session which saw it rise to 1.5580 marks and 116.33 yen in late trade after firmer U.S. asset markets prompted short-covering after Thursday's fall.

Dealers and analysts said the dollar's fortunes in the near term would continue to depend on the performance on the U.S. stock and bond markets. Any more strong data will only raise speculation of a credit tightening and if that hurts asset markets the dollar will fall.
Meanwhile, oil prices teetered from their highs despite Europe's big freeze as traders decided a bigger than expected rise in U.S. oil stocks was reason enough to take profits.
London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend dipped 30 cents to $23.92 a barrel in late trade.
CURRENCIES AT 1630 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.5580 marks and 116.33 yen, compared with 1.5407 and 115.47 in late trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 32.1 points higher at 4,089.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 25.79 at 2,282.76.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 10.51 at 2,859.28.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was closed at $362.15, down from the London's close on Thursday of $366.85.
